columns.name: Hardware platform
columns.instruction: Record the physical platform whose entanglement-generation link the source models or demonstrates. Select every platform the source treats in its own analysis. Choose 'Platform-agnostic / abstract model' when the source models links without a specific hardware platform.

columns.name: Multi-slot attempt-rate limiters
columns.instruction: Select every mechanism the source explicitly names as limiting how many entanglement-generation attempts can be made per unit time over many attempts or time slots. Count only overhead between or across attempts, not losses within one attempt. Select 'None stated' if the source names no such mechanism. Do not infer a mechanism from a keyword alone.

options.label: Source duty cycle or repetition rate
Limited communication qubits or bandwidth contention

columns.name: Single-attempt limits
columns.instruction: Quote or closely paraphrase what the source says limits the success probability or fidelity of one attempt, for example photon collection efficiency, fiber loss, detection efficiency or Bell-state measurement efficiency. Leave it unanswered if the source states no such limit.

columns.name: Attempt rate or repetition rate
columns.instruction: Record the rate of entanglement-generation attempts per unit time that the source states, as the source states it. If the source gives both an achieved rate and a projected rate, take the achieved rate. If the source states only an attempt duration, put the duration and its unit as stated. Leave it unanswered if the source states neither.

columns.name: Entanglement generation rate
columns.instruction: Record the heralded entanglement (Bell pair) generation rate the source reports for its main setting, as stated. If the source gives both a demonstrated rate and a projected rate, take the demonstrated one and note the projected one as context. Leave it unanswered for sources that report no rate.

columns.name: Mitigation of attempt-rate overhead
columns.instruction: Describe, close to the source's own words, any technique the source proposes or uses to raise the long-run attempt rate or to amortize overhead across attempts. Examples are faster state preparation, loading many atoms per cavity, multiplexing, optimized scheduling, and adaptive duty cycle. Write nothing if the source proposes no such technique.

columns.name: Study type
columns.instruction: Select the kind of evidence the source provides for its rate claims. Choose several only if the source both demonstrates experimentally and models or simulates the same link.

columns.name: Duty cycle or time budget quantified
columns.instruction: Answer yes if the source gives a quantitative breakdown of how time is shared across many attempts. Examples are the fraction of time spent attempting versus recooling, preparing, reloading or idling, or a duty cycle imposed by a detection-risk threshold. Answer no if it discusses rates without such a breakdown.

columns.name: Duty cycle or time budget quantified
columns.rationale: A quantified time budget shows directly how much each long-run mechanism limits the average attempt count.

column_suggestions.notes: Several rows are duplicate versions of the same work: the two 'Tools for Reducing Service Time' datasets, the two 'Electron juggling' records and the two 'Impact of Network Constraints' records. Compare them as one work, not as independent confirmation. Many rows are available only as abstracts, which may not state the mechanism details these columns ask for.
